questions.question: Does controlled reduction of oxygen partial pressure during SPS of the Ti-containing HEA suppress TiO precipitation while maintaining the 2709 MPa yield strength, or does it trigger BCC2 formation due to altered element segregation?
questions.rationale: The paper identifies TiO formation as a strength booster but also as a ductility reducer; controlling O2 is the only direct way to tune this trade-off.
questions.decision_use: Determines if a vacuum/low-O2 SPS protocol is viable to improve ductility without losing the 2709 MPa strength baseline.
answer_requirements: Compare yield strength and ductility of HEAs sintered at varying O2 partial pressures (e.g., 10^-3 to 10^-5 Pa)
Perform XRD and EDS to quantify TiO volume fraction and BCC2 phase presence
evidence_spans: However, it is inevitable that interstitial elements, such as O, N, etc. will be introduced during the preparing process, which will lead to the formation of precipitated phases [ [4] , [8] , [9] ].
the precipitated fine TiO particles are likely to impede the dislocation motion in the BCC matrix, thus increasing strength and slightly decreasing the ductility of the alloy

The excellent mechanical properties can be attributed to solid solution strengthening and grain boundary strengthening of the fine-grained BCC matrix, as well as the precipitation strengthening owing to the formation of TiO particles.

questions.question: Is the 707.5°C exothermic peak in DSC solely due to the FCC-to-monoclinic transformation of TiO, or does it indicate concurrent BCC-to-BCC2 phase separation driven by element segregation?
questions.rationale: Distinguishing between TiO phase transition and grain boundary segregation is critical for understanding the thermal stability of the BCC2 phase.
questions.decision_use: Guides the selection of heat treatment temperatures to stabilize or eliminate the BCC2 phase without degrading the TiO strengthening.
answer_requirements: Conduct high-temperature in-situ XRD at 707.5°C to identify the specific diffraction peaks appearing
Measure local elemental composition at grain boundaries using atom probe tomography (APT) before and after heating at 707.5°C
evidence_spans: Figure 1 d presents the DSC curve that an exothermic peak is obviously observed at 707.5 °C
It can be speculated that the formation of BCC2 results from the slightly inhomogeneous distribution of alloying elements at the grain boundaries of sintered HEA

The formation of TiO phase with FCC structure in the sintered sample indicated that the TiO phase remains in its original crystal structure at elevated temperature, due to the rapid cooling speed after SPS
